reasons: Deviation classification is sound: § 14.10 restricts only Customer's assignment and leaves IBM entirely unconstrained, so the clause fails the fallback's requirement that consent (not unreasonably withheld) apply to non-successor assignments on both sides — IBM could transfer to a Customer competitor without consent. This is a material, not cosmetic, gap.

Rationale correctly notes the absence of any Vendor change-of-control termination/re-pricing right, so walk-away is properly not asserted, and treats the narrower successor carve-out (no affiliate/asset-sale) as a secondary point rather than the sole basis.

Redline is directionally correct and actionable: it makes the restriction mutual with a not-unreasonably-withheld standard, bars assignment to a Customer competitor, and adds the affiliate and sale-of-substantially-all-assets carve-outs, reaching the preferred position without imposing any new burden on Customer (Customer already required consent).

Edit is confined to the one operative clause; the ~0.42 changed-character ratio reflects the mutuality rewrite the rule requires, and the void-assignment and continuing-liability sentences are preserved.
Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural with the [Playbook] prefix, and explains both what changed and why.
